### Summary

At the pin the corrected potential-energy work has no switch. `gravity-work: face` is the only gravity-work form,
and the work is booked wherever gravity is radial and the grid has an $x_1$ measure. This section keeps those gates
and the registered arms. The derivation of the corrected potential energy, the centroid slope and the implicit row
is in @sec-ch06-dwork and is not repeated here. With no switch there is no plain-budget control arm in a run. A
grid without a measure books the plain face work and warns.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Books the corrected potential-energy work of @eq-ch06-dwork-d.

**Data.** Radial density increment and grid faces in; energy increment out.

**Placement.** Gravity-work bookkeeping and the matching implicit operator.

**Activation.** Always when `grav1` is nonzero and the grid is `cartesian`, `spherical-polar` or
`gnomonic-equiangle`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Corrected budget on supported measures. Unsupported grids warn and book the plain face work.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-radial-exact-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathcal E = \sum_i V_i E_i + P$ is the corrected domain-integrated energy budget [J],
where $E_i$ is gas energy density [J m$^{-3}$], $V_i$[^rg-861cdfd13eb4] is cell volume [m$^3$] and $P$[^rg-859e2d0bb890] is the corrected potential
energy [J]; $g_1$ is radial acceleration [m s$^{-2}$].

### Derivation

See @sec-ch06-dwork for the corrected potential energy and the matching work. The chapter's check line `[C5]`
re-derives the cell-by-cell cancellation of the slope term for a fixed linear slope matrix
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}) holds three gates:
a gravity block with nonzero `grav1`, `gravity-work` equal to `face`, and a grid whose `x1_measure`
({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp x1_measure >}}) is not `none`. `x1_measure` is `plain` for `cartesian`, `radial`
for `spherical-polar` and `radial_mid` for `gnomonic-equiangle`. Any other value of `gravity-work`, and an active
`gravity-work-fixer`[^rg-a5b993b32d10], are refused when the deck is read (`ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) and again at setup. So the
second gate always holds.

At setup, `HydroImpl::reset` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}) warns once on a grid without a
measure and once on a periodic $x_1$ column. Neither warning changes the run. In `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) the corrected increment is added to the face gravity
work in one of two ways:

- **One block in $x_1$.** With `corrected_pe_work` ({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp corrected_pe_work >}}).
- **Across an $x_1$ seam.** With `corrected_pe_work_seam` ({{< code src/hydro/gravity_work.hpp corrected_pe_work_seam >}}).
  The neighbour's density change is exchanged, so a seam cell takes the centred slope of one block.

A periodic $x_1$ column has no $x_1$ neighbours in this sense and keeps the one-sided slope at its block edges. The
implicit solve couples the same corrected work when `radial_exact_work` holds and the block has at least three $x_1$
cells (`ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked`, {{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}).
An implicit scheme refuses an $x_1$ split, so the implicit row sees one block.

### Code

**How to use it.** Nothing needs to be set beyond gravity. Merge this fragment into a complete card with
non-periodic radial boundaries:

```yaml
geometry:
  type: cartesian
forcing:
  const-gravity:
    grav1: -9.8     # m s^-2
    gravity-work: face
```

`gravity-work: face` is the default and may be left out. Periodic radial boundaries and unsupported measures produce
warnings, not refusals. They do not establish the corrected-budget guarantee.

`HydroImpl::radial_exact_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}) contains this
selection step:

```cpp
  return g && g->grav1() != 0. && g->gravity_work() == "face" &&
         x1_measure(type) != X1Measure::none;
```

All three predicates must hold before the work in @eq-ch06-dwork-d is booked. `[C5]` checks its algebraic
cancellation for a fixed linear slope operator. It does not execute this C++ branch.

: Implementation sites for the corrected work. {#tbl-ch12-radial-exact-code}

1. Combine the gravity, work-mode and measure gates. The anchor `radial_exact_work` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}.
2. At setup, warn once on a grid without a measure and on a periodic $x_1$ column. The anchor
   `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}.
3. Add the corrected increment to the face work, with the seam form on a split column. The anchor `radial_exact`
   is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A grid without an $x_1$ measure keeps the plain face work, with only a warning. With no switch, a run cannot book the
plain face work on a supported grid for comparison. A lone gnomonic-equiangle block with reflecting lateral walls is
a mass-conservation question of the grid, not of this work (@sec-ch17). Split and unsplit $x_1$ columns agree except
on a periodic $x_1$ column, whose block edges keep the one-sided slope.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-861cdfd13eb4]: $V_i$ — cell volume

[^rg-859e2d0bb890]: $P$ — corrected discrete potential energy $\sum_iV_i[\rho_i\phi_i - g_1\sigma_i^2s_i[\rho]]$, exact to $O(h^4)$

[^rg-a5b993b32d10]: gravity-work-fixer — removed in V3: only `false` (the default) is accepted

[^rg-3ec07417d3f2]: $\mathcal E$ — the conserved energy functional of a scheme, named each time ($\mathcal E = \sum_iV_iE_i+P$ under D, $\sum_iV_iE_i+\mathrm{PE}_d$ under the plain face form)

[^rg-7da3ad6259c0]: VIC — vertically implicit correction
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
